id="spzA4HITppkogUZ7E6sR-3" parent="1" style="shape=rhombus;perimeter=rhombusPerimeter;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=center;" value="Includes" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="120" x="400" y="700" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="spzA4HITppkogUZ7E6sR-6" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="Notes + Modifications (Documentation):&nbsp;<br><ul><li>A `club_manager` can be a part of several clubs, and a club can contain (have) several club_managers. Therefore, this is a M:N relationship. However, a club MUST have a club_manager. Hence, this is a M:N relationship with total participation on the club_manager side.&nbsp;</li><li>Users can join multiple clubs, and Clubs can accommodate multiple Users. Users are required to join AT LEAST ONE club as per ClubTime! policy.&nbsp;</li><li>Users can &lt;share&gt; Clubs with other Users of a different club, or within their existing club (although that fulls under broadcast---like Announcement, Event Update, etc.). This action falls under the larger [Interaction] umbrella. Hence, (club) will be an attribute of Interaction rather than assigning it its own entity.&nbsp;</li><li>In my head, it makes sense for Users to be barred from sharing advertisement of another club, unless it is a broadcast allowed by a Club Manager or Admin.&nbsp;</li><li>interactionType includes share/like/comment/tags.&nbsp;</li><ul><li>I didn't want to make Share a separate relationship entity because it can fall under Interaction.&nbsp;</li></ul><li>Clubs can be managed by several Admins, and an Admin can oversee several Clubs. An Admin <i>must </i>manage AT LEAST one Club, and a Club <i>must </i>be managed by AT LEAST one Admin. Hence, this is a M:N total relationship.</li></ul>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="450" width="640" x="430" y="830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="spzA4HITppkogUZ7E6sR-8" parent="1" div.div:
Notes + Modifications (Documentation):
A `club_manager` can be a part of several clubs, and a club can contain (have) several club_managers. Therefore, this is a M:N relationship. However, a club MUST have a club_manager. Hence, this is a M:N relationship with total participation on the club_manager side.
Users can join multiple clubs, and Clubs can accommodate multiple Users. Users are required to join AT LEAST ONE club as per ClubTime! policy.
Users can <share> Clubs with other Users of a different club, or within their existing club (although that fulls under broadcast---like Announcement, Event Update, etc.). This action falls under the larger [Interaction] umbrella. Hence, (club) will be an attribute of Interaction rather than assigning it its own entity.
In my head, it makes sense for Users to be barred from sharing advertisement of another club, unless it is a broadcast allowed by a Club Manager or Admin.
interactionType includes share/like/comment/tags.
I didn't want to make Share a separate relationship entity because it can fall under Interaction.
Clubs can be managed by several Admins, and an Admin can oversee several Clubs. An Admin must manage AT LEAST one Club, and a Club must be managed by AT LEAST one Admin. Hence, this is a M:N total relationship.
